text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Elevated 5xx rate detected for prod-api (us-east) on route /v1/generate — errors spiked to ~18% over the last 5m, latency 95p > 2.5s. Paging maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): I'm on it. starting triage — can someone confirm customer impact? Julia?

julia (support): Customer reports a few realtime failures from our largest integration (AcmeCorp). They see timeouts and 502s intermittently, some requests return 500 with 'gateway: upstream timeout'. Impact: degraded feature for a subset of customers, not full outage.

liam (infra): Noted. Looking at gateway and ingress metrics — we have a surge of 504s at the ingress LB + a correlated increase in request queue length on gateway pods. No recent deploys in the last hour.

nora (sre): Heads up — trace drops across the traffic path. Datadog shows sampling rate for traces in prod-config was accidentally set to 0 in the last config rollout (probable config drift). That explains missing spans for affected requests.

maya (oncall): Ugh. Missing traces will slow down root cause. For live mitigation: 1) route traffic to fallback model-variant (lighter) to reduce backend latency, 2) enable temporary debug logs at edge to capture request IDs and upstream latencies, 3) roll a short-term rate limit on noisy clients. Assigning tasks: liam -> rollback sampling config + edge logging hotpatch, nora -> run customer impact checklist + add synthetic checks, julia -> notify impacted account owners with status.

liam (infra): Doing the config patch now. Patch commands I'm about to run (hotpatch):
```bash
# enable temp edge logging and restore trace sampling to 0.1
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/gateway GATEWAY_TEMP_LOG=1 TRACE_SAMPLING=0.1
# annotate to trigger a rolling update
kubectl -n prod patch deploy gateway --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"temp-debug":"true"}}}}}'
```

liam (infra): Running the patch. If gateway pods restart, expect a brief period of higher errors while they warm up — will coordinate with maya for traffic shift.

maya (oncall): I'm initiating traffic steering — shifting 30% of traffic to fallback variant (v1-quantized) and enabling circuit-breaker on the heavy request path. Command: `route-manager promote v1-quantized --percent=30 --path=/v1/generate`

incident-bot: pagerduty: incident acknowledged by maya (oncall). Severity: SEV2 — customer-visible degradation.

julia (support): Messaging drafted for AcmeCorp (will send after liam confirms sampling/edge logs). Draft: "We're seeing elevated errors for generation requests in US-East; on-call is mitigating. We'll update in 30 mins or earlier."

nora (sre): Observability gap notes: 
- traces missing because `TRACE_SAMPLING` was set to 0 by last config rollout (root cause of sparse traces).
- log ingress: log-shipper (cluster-ingester-3) has intermittent spikes in queue depth and dropped messages; not all errors are showing up in the logs.
- metrics present (error counts, latency histograms) but no spans/trace trees for slow requests.

nora (sre): Stopgap instrumentation plan (short-term):
- add `X-Debug-Req: <uuid>` header on edge for 5% of requests and log that header synchronously to stdout on gateway pods (low-latency log)
- emit a short-lived metric `edge.error_debug_count` with tags {path, upstream} via dogstatsd
- increase trace sampling to 10% once gateway is stable so we capture traces for slow requests

liam (infra): Implemented the env patch — rollout in progress. Gateway pods reporting `Ready` but seeing a transient spike in 502s while warm. Started synchronous stdout logging for debug header.

maya (oncall): Traffic steering succeeded, currently at 30% fallback. Early signal: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 9% on fallback segment; overall error rate down to ~11% and latency 95p at 1.9s. Good sign.

julia (support): Sent initial note to AcmeCorp. They replied, appreciate the update and asked for ETA. I gave 30m estimated mitigation window.

nora (sre): Added short-lived dashboard with new metric `edge.error_debug_count` and the debug header log stream. We can now correlate some failing request IDs with upstream response codes. Found a pattern: requests with empty `x-request-id` header correlate with a higher failure rate — looks like a client-side issue that surfaces as a gateway timeout when upstream retries happen.

maya (oncall): Good catch. Action: enforce `x-request-id` presence at edge for a short window and return 400 if missing to avoid expensive retries. That will remove noise and reduce load. Implementing now.

liam (infra): Patch applied to gateway to validate header. Also increased trace sampling to 0.1 (10%).

incident-bot: note: page escalation policy set to SEV2 responders.

maya (oncall): Summary / next steps:
- Immediate: continue routing to fallback (30%) until error rate < 5% for 10m.
- Short term (now->1h): keep edge debug logging and metric, collect traces, enforce x-request-id requirement, monitor customer impact, and prepare rollback plan.
- Postmortem: full RCA to include how TRACE_SAMPLING got set to 0 and why config rollout removed sampling (post-incident action).

julia (support): I'll follow up with AcmeCorp after the next status milestone.

nora (sre): Leaving this thread to update dashboards and capture the debug logs. If anyone wants to pair on trace analysis, ping me.

maya (oncall): Thanks team. If error rate resurges, I'll call for escalation. For now, keeping PD on-watch. :thumbsup:

(reacts: maya (oncall) :eyes:, liam (infra) :hammer:, nora (sre) :mag:)
